lines.text: Hundreds of notifications a day.
A text that says his bank account is blocked.
And it's exam week.
His phone knew all of it.
His AI agent knew none of it.
Until now.
Meet Arpit. A final-year student in Hamirpur, Himachal Pradesh.
Everything in his life lands on his phone first.
In October, India made over twenty-five billion UPI payments.
His bank texts him for every one.
The average Indian sees thirteen scam messages a day.
And since twenty twenty-one, Indians have reported over fifty-five thousand crore rupees in cyber fraud.
His agent lives on his laptop, a foot away.
And it can't see any of it.
So Arpit built the fix. Phone Senses.
A Hermes plugin that gives his agent the senses of his own phone.
No screen tapping. It talks to Android directly, through Termux.
And it always asks before it touches anything.
Here's his real day, on his real phone.
Morning. One question: give me my phone brief.
Hermes reads what his phone sees, and puts the scam text right at the top.
One-time codes stay hidden. When Hermes tried to reveal one, it had to ask. Nobody said yes, so it stayed hidden.
Where did his money go? Every bank SMS, sorted by category.
And every rupee that came in by UPI.
Bills before they're late, and subscriptions, added up for the month.
Then the text that almost got him. Hermes flags it, and shows why.
Text Mom: I'll call you after the exam.
Hermes stops, and shows the exact words.
Allow once. It goes from his own SIM.
One more text? He changes his mind. Deny. Nothing is sent, and Hermes doesn't try again.
Then a stranger calls about his bank account, and asks him to install AnyDesk. Hermes connects the dots, and the phone warns him out loud.
A watch rule catches the delivery text, just once.
Battery under twenty? He'll get a heads-up.
That night, the phone is gone. Under the bed.
One line to Hermes. It rings, speaks, vibrates and flashes.
Follow one real request: what's my battery?
The approval hook checks it first. A read passes.
The request is signed with a secret that's never sent.
A one-time nonce stops anyone replaying it.
In Termux, a tiny helper asks Android directly.
And the answer is back in about a second and a half.
Before: hundreds of notifications, and an agent that couldn't see them.
Now: one question, and Hermes knows his whole day.
It reads the phone itself, not pictures of the screen.
Texts, calls, photos and codes: all four ask him first.
Codes stay hidden. The plugin talks only to his phone.
Phone Senses. Your phone's senses, for Hermes.
And it still asks before it touches anything.
Built by Arpit Singh, in Hamirpur. Open source, for Hermes Agent.
